verified.edge: M. Run-up from the pre-deal base: $8.36 (2026-10-26 close) to $9.91 today = +18.5%, about 61% of the move to deal value is already taken. Remaining: $9.91 to $10.875 (0.5196 x ARCC $18.60 + $1.21) = +9.7% gross. Carry is positive: MFIC pays $0.31/qtr against about $0.25 of ARCC dividend per hedge ratio. The market is pricing something: a likely NAV-based adjustment to the exchange ratio after MFIC's NAV fell 3.8% to $12.86, a long timeline, or break risk. Unresolved, that keeps the edge at M, not H.
verified.primary_source: Business Wire, 'Ares Capital Corporation Agrees to Acquire MidCap Financial Investment Corporation', 2026-10-27; MFIC Q3-2026 results (GlobeNewswire, 2026-11-05: NAV $12.86, -3.8%, $10.88 = $9.67 ARCC stock + $1.21 cash); FMP EOD prices MFIC/ARCC to 2026-11-19
verified.analysis: The deal is real, dated and unfired. Today's spread is about 9.7% gross against the ARCC ratio, not thin as triage assumed. MFIC $9.91 vs implied $10.875 at ARCC $18.60, ratio inferred as $9.67 / $18.61 (the 2026-10-26 ARCC close) = about 0.5196. KEY GAP: the exact exchange-ratio mechanics could not be verified. The ARCC release returned 403 and the web-search budget was used up. If the ratio is NAV-for-NAV, fixed at closing (common in BDC deals), then the 3.8% NAV markdown in Q3 and any further credit losses before close come straight out of the consideration. That would explain the wide spread, and the true remaining capture could be well under 9.7%. Downside on a break is about $8.0-8.4 (pre-deal $8.36, with NAV lower since), roughly -16%, against about +9.7% upside. Reward/risk is under 1 before probability weighting. Plaintiff-firm 'investigations' are routine and do not change this. Keep WATCH. Upgrade only after the S-4 confirms a fixed exchange ratio and gives a closing timeline.

It traded at $25.52 at end-July and peaked at $45. It now sits at $14.16, 2% above its 52-week low of $13.72, below its 50-day ($21.7) and 200-day ($25.9) averages. The setup is washed out, not run up. (b) Remaining to a favorable resolution: about +40-60%. My rough re-derived approval-branch value is about $20-22 a share: net cash of about $5.9/sh plus the launch franchise at about 2.5-3x an $800M peak, haircut for Pharmakon debt costs and dilution. The stale street $43 and our earlier $38 approval-branch figure both predate Baxfendy's slow launch and are not used. The CRL branch is about $6-7, net cash after burn, roughly -55%. Approval is probably about 85-90% likely, so the PDUFA itself is mostly priced as approval. The asymmetry sits in the launch ramp, not the decision. Probability-weighted value is about $19-20, roughly 1.1:1 reward to risk. The washed-out tape is real but does not create a dated edge on its own.

verified.analysis: The catalyst is real, dated and forward. The PDUFA of 2026-12-22 was reaffirmed in the Q3 release on 2026-11-04, and new AHA data on 2026-11-08 showed blood pressure lowering holding through 48 weeks. The binary is largely de-risked: positive Phase 3 and the same drug class already approved in Baxfendy (2026-05-18). The price collapse from $45 to $14 reflects worry about second-to-market economics: AstraZeneca's cardiorenal reach, step-therapy barriers and a slow class ramp. Approval alone therefore probably re-rates the stock only modestly. Capital-structure check from the Q3 10-Q balance sheet (2026-09-30): $624.7M of cash and investments against $98.3M of senior secured Pharmakon debt gives about $526M net, about $5.9/sh on about 88.6M shares. No preferred stock. Up to $265M of Tanabe commercial milestones is contingent on sales. Net cash supports a CRL floor near $6-7 and an approval value around $20-22, so the equity can carry the flagged upside but only at about 1:1 odds, and the edge depends on launch execution. Gaps: the web-search budget was exhausted, so no current consensus target, short interest or options-implied move was checked. Approval probability is my estimate, not sourced.
